doctrine: Every ELIGIBLE PUBLIC product URL is also a native-app acquisition and continuation surface.
The canonical public URL is the identity. There is no separate SEO, share or app identity.
Native acquisition must never become a forced interstitial. Public web stays usable.
Opening from a public object must reach THAT destination, never merely app home.
Knowledge of a URL is not authorization. Continuation never widens what a visitor may see.
Platforms do not independently invent eligibility. This file is the only source.

objectFamilies.note: Bare /p/:id is the catch-all. It MUST be matched last or it swallows every prefixed family below.
Must be tried before ANNOUNCEMENT: 'a' is a prefix of 'art' only if matching is done on characters rather than whole segments. Whole-segment matching is required.
Meeting admission is decided by the meeting's own authority. Reaching the join surface is not admission.

include.why: The canonical public share family. This is the identity people actually send.
Public post reading; the destination /p/:id resolves to.
Guest-reachable meeting entry. NOT /join/ -- that path is declared by no router and fails closed to MEMBER, which put a login wall in front of invited guests.
Invitation acceptance; continuation depends on it.
Auth ceremonies that complete a preserved destination.

exclude.why: Authoring, not reading. A public sibling never implies its editor is public.

platformLimits.android: Intent filters express pathPrefix, never negation. Excludes are enforced in-app by the resolver and by route classification, not by the manifest.
platformLimits.ios: AASA supports explicit exclusion, so the excludes above are expressed there directly.
platformLimits.windows: App URI Handlers associate a HOST, not a path. All path scoping is enforced in-app.

acquisition.androidDistributionNote: Play production access has NOT been granted; the app is in closed testing. A general visitor cannot obtain it from that link, so Android must not be advertised as generally available.

destinationPreservation.rule: A destination is preserved ACROSS the auth boundary and resumed after it. It is never discarded, and never widened: resuming only re-attempts the destination under the visitor's real authority.

review.note: PRODUCT FEEDBACK is first-party governed Aura feedback. RATE/REVIEW is the platform-owned mechanism. They are never merged.
review.eligibility: Follows meaningful successful use. Subordinate to acquisition, never the primary call to action.

platformContinuation._note: associationConfigured describes THIS SOURCE TREE. shippedInClient describes the client a visitor actually has installed. They are separate because the web surface deploys before the native clients do, and an "Open in Aura" shown against a client that cannot route the destination is a fake Open state -- it opens the old app at home and loses the very thing the person tapped. Flip shippedInClient only when a released client carries the continuation capability.

windows.mechanism: App URI Handlers + aura:// protocol activation, resolved from launch arguments

webAcquisition._note: Eligibility is the association scope, not a second hand-kept list. The previous surface listed exact static paths only, so marketing pages offered the app and the object pages people actually share offered nothing -- precisely backwards.
